mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for new construction, which typically precedes positive equity market returns as economic activity accelerates. This relationship holds consistently across business cycles with minimal regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST rises by at least 0.5% in the prior month, or the correlation between HOUST growth and SPX returns is negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces liquidity and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the average 5-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive equity returns over 60 days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS and INDPRO rising fails to predict positive 60-day returns when the correlation between the two series and SPX returns is negative, or the average 60-day return in these instances is not significantly positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), reduced liquidity and higher discount rates typically cause negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the average return in these cycles is not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing output, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days as economic momentum accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO rises by at least 0.3% in the prior month, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 5.0%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%, or the average 20-day return in these instances is not significantly positive (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates aggressive monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: The joint signal of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS rising fails to predict negative 60-day returns when the correlation between the two series and SPX returns is positive, or the average 60-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising residential mortgage applications (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) signal strong household spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days as economic momentum peaks.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the average 5-day return in these instances is not significantly positive (p-value > 0.05).
